# origin dns commands

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py from `origin --help` of the release scripts/origin-cli.version pins (v1.19.0).
     Do not edit by hand: fix the help text in origincloudhq/cli, or scripts/cli_reference_overrides.yml, and rerun. -->

This page lists every `origin dns` command. Hosted zones belong to a project and to no region. `--hosted-zone` names a hosted zone; `--zone` is an availability zone, the one of the Floating IP an alias follows. For the options every `origin` command accepts, see [Global options](../../platform/reference/cli.md#global-options); for how `--project`, `--zone` and `--region` default, see [Use the CLI](../../platform/access/cli.md#set-a-default-project-zone-and-region).

## origin dns

DNS: hosted zones, public or private, their record sets, and the VPCs a private zone is attached to. Hosted zones are a project's (`--project`), the same in every region; `--hosted-zone` names one, while `--zone` is an availability zone, that of a Floating IP an alias answers with. A public zone answers on the internet once its name is delegated to the name servers `get-hosted-zone` shows, and becomes `ACTIVE` once the TXT record its challenge names answers where the name is hosted now (`verify-hosted-zone` checks it at once). A private zone answers in the VPCs it is attached to, each a VPC of the zone's project.

Every `origin dns` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host, `https://dns.origincloudapis.eu`, the same in every region. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_DNS_ENDPOINT`. |

### get-hosted-zone

Returns a hosted zone.

```sh
origin dns get-hosted-zone [OPTIONS] --hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | yes | The zone to return. Its id, completed with `--project`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/hostedZones/{hosted_zone}`. |

### list-hosted-zones

Lists a project's hosted zones, oldest first.

```sh
origin dns list-hosted-zones [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most zones to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--dns-name <DNS_NAME>` | no | Only the zones of this domain, written as `--dns-name` is; every zone when left empty. |

### create-hosted-zone

Creates a hosted zone, empty. A public zone starts `PENDING_VERIFICATION`, with the token to publish in `challenge`; a private zone starts `ACTIVE`. Refused with `BAD_REQUEST` for a name the platform keeps for itself, or once the project's or organization's quota of zones is used up, and with `PAYMENT_METHOD_REQUIRED` while the project has no valid billing.

```sh
origin dns create-hosted-zone [OPTIONS] --dns-name <DNS_NAME> --visibility <VISIBILITY>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--dns-name <DNS_NAME>` | yes | The domain, such as `example.com`, without the final dot; answered in lowercase. A public zone's has at least two labels and at most 235 characters, so its challenge name fits. A private zone's may have one label, but isn't `internal` or a name below it, which answer each instance's own name. Neither is one of the platform's own domains or a name below one. |
| `--visibility <VISIBILITY>` | yes | Where the zone is answered. Possible values: `PUBLIC`, `PRIVATE`. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | no | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id within a day returns the zone the first request created, as it is now, instead of creating a second one. One is generated when not given. |

### update-hosted-zone

Changes a hosted zone's tags.

```sh
origin dns update-hosted-zone [OPTIONS] --hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE> <--tag <KEY=VALUE>|--no-tags>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | yes | The hosted zone to change. Its id, completed with `--project`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/hostedZones/{hosted_zone}`. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | one of `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-tags` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-tags` | one of `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Remove all of its tags. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id within a day returns the zone as it is now, instead of changing it again. One is generated when not given. |

### delete-hosted-zone

Deletes a hosted zone. Refused with `CONFLICT` while it holds record sets or, for a private zone, VPC attachments: delete them first.

```sh
origin dns delete-hosted-zone [OPTIONS] --hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | yes | The zone to delete. Its id, completed with `--project`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/hostedZones/{hosted_zone}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id within a day succeeds as the first did, instead of answering `NOT_FOUND`. One is generated when not given. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### verify-hosted-zone

Checks a public zone's challenge now, instead of waiting for the platform's next check, and returns the zone as it is then, with the check's outcome in `challenge.last_check`. A pending zone whose token answers becomes `ACTIVE`, and so does a suspended one while its name is free; otherwise the zone stays as it was. A call within 30 seconds of the zone's last check answers with that check's outcome and asks the name's DNS nothing. Refused with `NOT_FOUND` once a pending zone's window has ended, which deleted it, and with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, retryable, when the name's DNS didn't answer in time or too many checks are under way. A private zone has no challenge, and is refused with `BAD_REQUEST`. Checking an active zone changes nothing, so a client may repeat the call.

```sh
origin dns verify-hosted-zone [OPTIONS] --hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | yes | The public zone to verify. Its id, completed with `--project`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/hostedZones/{hosted_zone}`. |

Returns a record set.

```sh

```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | no | The `{hosted_zone}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--record-set` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--record-set <RECORD_SET>` | yes | The record set to return. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--hosted-zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/hostedZones/{hosted_zone}/recordSets/{record_set}`. |

### list-record-sets

Lists a zone's record sets by `--dns-name`, then by `--type`.

```sh
origin dns list-record-sets [OPTIONS] --hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | yes | The `{hosted_zone}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most record sets to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--dns-name <DNS_NAME>` | no | Only the record sets of this name, written as `--dns-name` is; every name's when left empty. |
| `--type <TYPE>` | no | Only the record sets of this type; every type's when left unset. Possible values: `A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `TXT`, `MX`, `SRV`, `CAA`. |

### create-record-set

Creates a record set. Refused with `CONFLICT` when the zone holds a record set of that name and type, or when a CNAME would share its name. Refused with `BAD_REQUEST` for a name outside the zone, a value its type doesn't take, an alias to a Floating IP outside the zone's project, or once the project's or organization's quota of record sets is used up. An alias to a Floating IP that was created moments ago may be refused with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, retryable.

```sh
origin dns create-record-set [OPTIONS] --hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE> --dns-name <DNS_NAME> --type <TYPE> <--basic-json <JSON>|--alias <KEY=VALUE,...>|--alias-json <JSON>>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | yes | The `{hosted_zone}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--dns-name <DNS_NAME>` | yes | The name the records answer for: the zone's `--dns-name` or a name below it, written in full, such as `www.example.com`, without the final dot; answered in lowercase. Labels may hold `_` (`_dmarc.example.com`), and `*` only as the whole leftmost label, for a wildcard. |
| `--type <TYPE>` | yes | The records' type. An alias is `A`. Possible values: `A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `TXT`, `MX`, `SRV`, `CAA`. |
| `--ttl <DURATION>` | no | How long resolvers may keep the answer, from 30 seconds to 7 days, in whole seconds. 300 seconds when left out. Such as `30s` or `1m`. |
| `--basic-json <JSON>` | one of `--basic-json`, `--alias`, `--alias-json` | Values of its own. As the API's JSON, an object whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. One of `--basic-json`, `--alias`: give exactly one. |
| `--alias <KEY=VALUE,...>` | one of `--basic-json`, `--alias`, `--alias-json` | The address of a platform resource, followed as it changes. As comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs. A key is a field's name, with `_` or `-`. The keys: `floating_ip`, required: The Floating IP whose address the record set answers with, in the zone's project. A Floating IP's address is an IPv4 address, so the record set is of type `A`; an `AAAA` alias is refused. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/floatingIps/{floating_ip}`. A value with a comma in it goes through `--alias-json` too. One of `--basic-json`, `--alias`: give exactly one. |
| `--alias-json <JSON>` | one of `--basic-json`, `--alias`, `--alias-json` | As the API's JSON, an object whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. A resource name in a field of the message itself is completed with `--project` and `--zone`, as in its KEY=VALUE form; one nested deeper must be whole. Instead of `--alias`. One of `--basic-json`, `--alias`: give exactly one. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id within a day returns the record set the first request created, as it is now, instead of being refused as a conflict. One is generated when not given. |

### update-record-set

Replaces a record set's TTL or what it answers with: `--ttl`, `--basic-json` or `--alias`, or `*`. Naming one kind in `updateMask` replaces the kind the record set had. With `*`, a TTL left out keeps the record set's; naming `--ttl` without one sets the default, 300 seconds. Its name and type stay; another type is a new record set.

```sh
origin dns update-record-set [OPTIONS] --record-set <RECORD_SET> <--ttl <DURATION>|--basic-json <JSON>|--alias <KEY=VALUE,...>|--alias-json <JSON>>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | no | The `{hosted_zone}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--record-set` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--record-set <RECORD_SET>` | yes | The record set to change. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--hosted-zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/hostedZones/{hosted_zone}/recordSets/{record_set}`. |
| `--ttl <DURATION>` | one of `--ttl`, `--basic-json`, `--alias`, `--alias-json` | How long resolvers may keep the answer, from 30 seconds to 7 days, in whole seconds. 300 seconds when left out. Such as `30s` or `1m`. Left as it is when not given. |
| `--basic-json <JSON>` | one of `--ttl`, `--basic-json`, `--alias`, `--alias-json` | Values of its own. As the API's JSON, an object whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. It is replaced whole: a key not given is reset. Left as it is when none of these is given. One of `--basic-json`, `--alias`: give at most one. Setting it replaces whichever of them is set. |
| `--alias <KEY=VALUE,...>` | one of `--ttl`, `--basic-json`, `--alias`, `--alias-json` | The address of a platform resource, followed as it changes. As comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs. A key is a field's name, with `_` or `-`. The keys: `floating_ip`, required: The Floating IP whose address the record set answers with, in the zone's project. A Floating IP's address is an IPv4 address, so the record set is of type `A`; an `AAAA` alias is refused. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/floatingIps/{floating_ip}`. A value with a comma in it goes through `--alias-json` too. It is replaced whole: a key not given is reset. Left as it is when none of these is given. One of `--basic-json`, `--alias`: give at most one. Setting it replaces whichever of them is set. |
| `--alias-json <JSON>` | one of `--ttl`, `--basic-json`, `--alias`, `--alias-json` | As the API's JSON, an object whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. A resource name in a field of the message itself is completed with `--project` and `--zone`, as in its KEY=VALUE form; one nested deeper must be whole. Instead of `--alias`. It is replaced whole: a key not given is reset. Left as it is when none of these is given. One of `--basic-json`, `--alias`: give at most one. Setting it replaces whichever of them is set. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id within a day returns the record set as the first request left it, instead of changing it again. One is generated when not given. |


| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | no | The `{hosted_zone}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--record-set` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--record-set <RECORD_SET>` | yes | The record set to delete. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--hosted-zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/hostedZones/{hosted_zone}/recordSets/{record_set}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id within a day succeeds as the first did, instead of answering `NOT_FOUND`. One is generated when not given. |

### batch-change-record-sets

Deletes, replaces and creates record sets of one zone together, all or none. The zone is checked as the changes leave it, not after each change, so a CNAME may take the place of the A record set it replaces in one call. A batch makes 1 to 1000 changes, and names a record set once at most across `--deletion` and `--updates-json`. Each change is refused as its own method would refuse it, naming the change; then none is made.

```sh
origin dns batch-change-record-sets [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | no | The `{hosted_zone}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--deletion` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--deletion <RECORD_SET>` | no | The record sets to delete, by name. Each by its id, completed with `--project` and `--hosted-zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/hostedZones/{hosted_zone}/recordSets/{record_set}`. Repeat for more. |
| `--updates-json <JSON>` | no | The record sets to change, each with the fields to change, as `UpdateRecordSet` takes them. The whole list as the API's JSON, an array of objects whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. |
| `--creations-json <JSON>` | no | The record sets to create, as `CreateRecordSet` takes them. The whole list as the API's JSON, an array of objects whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id within a day answers with the record sets the first request changed and created, as they are now, instead of making the changes again. One is generated when not given. |

### get-vpc-attachment


| Option | Required | Description |

### list-vpc-attachments

Lists a private zone's VPC attachments, oldest first. With `-` for the zone, lists every zone's in the project, which with `--vpc` finds the zones attached to a VPC.

```sh
origin dns list-vpc-attachments [OPTIONS] --hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | yes | The `{hosted_zone}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most attachments to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--vpc <VPC>` | no | Only the attachments to this VPC; every VPC's when left empty. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/vpcs/{vpc}`. |

### create-vpc-attachment

Attaches a private zone to a VPC of the zone's project. Refused with `BAD_REQUEST` for a public zone, or for a VPC that isn't in the zone's project, with the same words whichever project it is in. Refused with `CONFLICT` when the VPC holds an attached zone of the same name. A VPC created moments ago may be refused with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, retryable. The VPC's instances resolve the zone's names once the VPC's hosts serve the zone.

```sh
origin dns create-vpc-attachment [OPTIONS] --hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE> --vpc <VPC>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | yes | The `{hosted_zone}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--vpc <VPC>` | yes | The VPC the zone answers in, in the zone's project. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/vpcs/{vpc}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id within a day returns the attachment the first request created, as it is now, instead of being refused as a conflict. One is generated when not given. |

### delete-vpc-attachment

Detaches a private zone from a VPC. The VPC's instances stop resolving the zone's names once the VPC's hosts drop the zone.

```sh
origin dns delete-vpc-attachment [OPTIONS] --vpc-attachment <VPC_ATTACHMENT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--hosted-zone <HOSTED_ZONE>` | no | The `{hosted_zone}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--vpc-attachment` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--vpc-attachment <VPC_ATTACHMENT>` | yes | The attachment to delete. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--hosted-zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/hostedZones/{hosted_zone}/vpcAttachments/{vpc_attachment}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id within a day succeeds as the first did, instead of answering `NOT_FOUND`. One is generated when not given. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |
